findings.title: Referer-based host check is spoofable and breaks when referer is absent (e.g. HTTPS->HTTP, privacy extensions)
findings.body: ensure_embeddable relies entirely on request.referer to validate the embedding host. The Referer header is client-controlled and often stripped by browsers/proxies for privacy reasons, so legitimate embeds can be blocked (DoS on themselves) while an attacker that can control/spoof the Referer header (e.g. via a crafted request from a page that sets referrer policy, or environments where referer leaks) could pass this check. A more robust mechanism (e.g. signed state, or Origin header combined with Referer, with graceful fallback) should be used instead of trusting Referer alone for access control.

findings.title: import silently returns nil on invalid URL without raising/logging
findings.body: self.import returns unless url matches http(s) scheme, silently discarding content/title and not informing callers (PollFeed, disqus.thor) that an item was skipped. In PollFeed#poll_feed, rss.items.each calls TopicEmbed.import without checking the return value, so malformed feed URLs are silently dropped with no logging, making debugging feed import failures hard.

findings.title: mutates shared content string before computing checksum, and unescapes untrusted HTML without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import mutates its `contents` argument in place via `contents << ...` to append the import footer (topic_embed.rb line 13), and poll_feed passes `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` built fresh each iteration, so this isn't a major issue here, but combined with `absolutize_urls`, raw remote HTML content from an RSS feed is directly rendered with cook_method raw_html and never sanitized (no `sanitize` gem usage), meaning any HTML/JS in the feed content is stored and rendered as-is in the post. This creates a stored-XSS-like risk since posts imported this way bypass the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline entirely (Post#cook returns raw for cook_method raw_html).

findings.title: Raw HTML cook_method bypasses all sanitization for embedded/imported content
findings.body: Post#cook returns `raw` unmodified when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText/Plugin::Filter sanitization entirely. Since this path is used for RSS-imported and readability-imported content (see TopicEmbed.import / import_remote), any malicious markup in third-party feeds or scraped pages will be stored and served as-is to viewers, enabling XSS through the embed feature if the imported site/feed is compromised or malicious.

findings.title: No rate limiting/validation on embed_url triggering background job for arbitrary URLs
findings.body: The `best` action enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url supplied by the client as long as referer host matches embeddable_host, but the embed_url itself can be any value (TopicRetriever later checks host, but only after the job runs). This means arbitrary users can trigger outbound HTTP fetches (potential SSRF-ish behavior / resource exhaustion) merely by hitting this endpoint many times with different query strings, since the per-URL throttle key is only enforced inside TopicRetriever and not before enqueueing the job each time `best` is hit for a brand new distinct URL.
